> The pack: do the writable volumes keep littlefs?
> 
> 1. The read-only system volume moves to the pack (docs/servers/packd.md), a format that cannot be written. The writable volumes (fsd:data with the homes, and the labelled vault volumes) still need a file system that handles commits, power loss and a worn medium. Do they keep littlefs?
>    - Yes, littlefs stays for writable volumes (recommended): Recommended. littlefs is built for a written medium; its cost showed only on the boot's 2,000 whole-object reads, which the pack now takes. fsd and libs/littlefs change nothing in PACK1. BOOT1 drops littlefs's read cache: no measurement says a session's file reads need one.
>    - Replace littlefs everywhere, later: A second format for writable volumes, designed when evidence asks for it (a package of its own, not PACK1). Until then littlefs stays; this option only records the intent.
>    - Keep littlefs and build its read cache anyway: BOOT1's dropped step 2 (the reference's rcache and a CTZ cursor in libs/littlefs) is built for the writable volumes without a measurement asking for it. Costs a change to the writable path's library for an unmeasured gain.
